main_text.p: nius lib. de Orat.I. his uerbis est complexus: Existere autē “controuersias etiam ex scripti interpretatione, in quo “aut ambiguè quid sit scriptū, “aut contrariè, aut ita ut à sententia scriptū dissideat. Ex “uerbo, cùm id propter ipsius “ambiguam ancipitemque significationem definitione aperiendū est. Aliam enim esse cōtrouersiam quæ ex uerbo, aliam quę ex scripto nascitur, Cicero in Partitionibus his demonstrat uerbis: Hoc “genus, inquit, quod ex scripto “nascitur, ne in definitionem “quidem uenit. Nam etiamsi “uerbū aliquod de scripto de- “fi-

page.notes: The right-margin marks are printed quotation marks ("“") repeated beside each line of the quoted passage; they are transcribed as notes. Line-end "de-" and final "fi-" are a word split across lines; the full word is not visible on this page, so it is kept as printed. The text continues on the next page. Faint marks and stains in the margin are not printed text and are left out. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout.
